overview: This file consists of a Department of State list-of-papers sheet for the subject “Base Metals—Japan.” It indexes correspondence involving Harold Hochschild about Japan’s requirements for lead, copper, and zinc—identified as important munitions metals—and a report associated with Werner concerning aluminum production in Taiwan. The sheet also indicates that an incoming letter was recorded under decimal-file classification 894.24.

subfiles.about: An archival index sheet lists correspondence on Japan’s requirements for lead, copper, and zinc and a report on aluminum production in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records correspondence involving Harold Hochschild concerning Japan’s requirements for the principal non-ferrous metals used in munitions: lead, copper, and zinc. It references a letter of February 25 and an apparent related entry dated March 1, 1932, while noting that the incoming communication was filed under 894.24. A second item, apparently associated with Werner and dated December 9, 1938, reports on aluminum production in Taiwan; the OCR leaves portions of the tabular metadata uncertain.

interest: The sheet is useful for reconstructing documents that may be missing from this surviving file and for tracing related correspondence through the State Department’s decimal filing system. Its entries connect assessments of Japan’s munitions-metal requirements with aluminum production in colonial Taiwan, offering leads for research into Japanese strategic-resource planning during the 1930s. The cross-reference to file 894.24 is especially valuable for locating the associated incoming letter.
